University College Dublin, Ireland
UCD School of Sociology - UCD Geary Institute for Public Policy
Fully Funded PhD Position

Project: From Human Capital to Intelligence Management: Data-driven Economy and Brain-Computer Interfaces (IMR)
Funding: European Research Council ERC Starting Grant
Supervisor: Associate Professor Edemilson Paraná

About the project:
Join one of Europe’s leading research programmes on neurotechnology, AI and society. The ERC-funded IMR project explores the implications of neurotechnology for labour and society. It investigates Brain-Computer Interfaces BCIs as sociotechnical systems embedded within transformations of the digital economy.
The PhD will contribute to the sociological investigation of the sociotechnical production of intelligence in computational neuroscience and brain research, especially BCI technologies. You will examine how initiatives like the US BRAIN Initiative and the EU Human Brain Project produce and circulate knowledge about the brain, BCIs and AI.

What We Offer:
- 4 years full PhD funding in accordance with ERC and UCD regulations - €30,000 tax-free stipend per annum, with waived tuition fees
- Outstanding interdisciplinary research environment within the UCD School of Sociology and the UCD Geary Institute for Public Policy
- Opportunities for international fieldwork and/or research visits in Europe and the United States
- Funding for conference participation and/or research training/professional development
- Collaboration with an international network of leading scholars in sociology, Science and Technology Studies, political economy, digital sociology and more

Duties and Responsibilities:
- Produce an original article-based PhD dissertation within the framework of the ERC-funded IMR project
- Conduct documentary and archival research, qualitative document analysis, semi-structured interviews and comparative fieldwork
- Contribute to collaborative publications, conference presentations and other research outputs
- Participate actively in research group activities including seminars, reading groups and collaborative meetings
- Assist with organisation of workshops, conferences, public engagement activities
- Contribute to project communication and dissemination including website and social media content

Person Specification:
Applicants should hold a degree in Sociology or a closely related discipline, including Anthropology, Political Economy, Communication, or other relevant social science fields.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
- Excellent qualitative research skills, particularly document analysis, interviewing and ethnographical observation
- Excellent written and spoken English CEFR Level C1
- Ability to work independently while contributing to collaborative research
- Strong organisational, communication and project management skills
- Commitment to producing high-quality international research outputs
- Enthusiasm for comparative and international research

Advantageous but not essential: Experience with qualitative data analysis software e.g. NVivo, MAXQDA, http://ATLAS.ti

Application Procedure:
Submit:
- Cover letter outlining motivation and suitability max 2 pages
- Curriculum vitae max 3 pages
- Research statement describing intended dissertation project, work in progress, plans for publication, and academic goals max 3 pages
- Writing sample e.g. dissertation chapter, journal article max 30 pages
- Certified academic transcripts and degree certificates
